locator: I q.3 a.7 co., fourth proof: in omni composito oportet esse potentiam et actum
interpretation: Every composite has potency and act, because one part is act relative to another or all parts are as in potency to the whole. Only the potency is used, attributed to the composite in some respect. 'Composite' is an abstract predicate; the first proof's enumeration of compositions (a.1-a.6) is not formalized.
